message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. He was born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, and rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School. Drafted first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003, he quickly became a dominant force in the NBA.

James has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), Miami Heat (2010–2014), and Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). He has won four NBA championships—two with Miami (2012, 2013), one with Cleveland (2016), and one with Los Angeles (2020)—and earned four NBA Finals MVP awards. In addition to his championship success, he has been named NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) four times (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and has been selected to the All‑NBA First Team 13 times.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the “I Promise” program, which supports at-risk youth in his hometown. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment, and starring in movies such as *Space Jam: A New Legacy* (2021).
